solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Senior officer in underwear lounged around hotel

parts.note: bras are items of women's underwear

indicators.note: the word for lounged goes around the hotel letter

parts.note: lounged about means sat
H is Hotel in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A high-ranking officer caught lounging in his underwear in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the lounging word round the hotel letter; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hat is informal British slang for a high-ranking military officer, from the gold braid on the cap.

clue.text: Marked as criminal, but not with own label

definitions.meaning: to be stigmatised, publicly labelled as a wrongdoer
... goods carry a maker's name, unlike a supermarket's own-label products

explanation.surface: Someone stigmatised as a crook, yet sold without a personal label.
explanation.walkthrough: Own-label goods are those a shop sells under its own name; the alternative is a branded product.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from a brand as a mark burnt or printed on: one a stigma, the other a trade name.

clue.text: Lovely piece of work, are you?

definitions.meaning: a fine painting or sculpture is a work of ...
in old English, 'thou ...' was the form for 'you are'

explanation.surface: A flattering question: are you a lovely piece of work?
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is archaic grammar: 'art thou?' means 'are you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings and sculpture are art; and art is the old second-person form of the verb to be.

clue.text: Cage, metal, in dry lake

indicators.note: the cage and metal words are placed inside the word for dry

parts.note: sere means dry or withered
a pen is an enclosure for animals
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A list of odd items: a cage and some metal sitting in a dried-up lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serpentine is the ornamental lake in London's Hyde Park, a specific example of a lake.

clue.text: Be suffering? Take on the Bible for help

indicators.note: the word for be suffering takes on the Bible abbreviation in front of it

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible
to ail is to be unwell or suffer

explanation.surface: Someone in distress is advised to turn to the Bible for help.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in 'of no avail', so it can stand for help.

clue.text: No end of reason to keep policeman a university place

indicators.note: the trimmed reason word keeps the policeman inside it
the last letter of the word for reason is dropped

parts.note: a cause is a reason
MP is a military policeman

explanation.surface: Without end of reason to keep a policeman, the university grounds are unguarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' trims the last letter, and 'to keep' wraps the trimmed word round the military policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: One delivering big service tree

definitions.meaning: in tennis a player who serves aces is an ace server

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a made-up word: one who serves aces in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples; the first sense is a whimsical coinage for someone serving aces.

clue.text: Profits secure in good transactions

indicators.note: the profits word secures the other two pieces by holding them inside

parts.note: proceeds are the money made from a sale

explanation.surface: Good dealings ensure the profits are safely locked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secure' places the two short pieces just before the final S of the profits word.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceedings are the business conducted at a meeting, or legal actions: a record of transactions.

clue.text: One cutting small member of audience?

parts.note: an audience is made up of people who hear

explanation.surface: A curious question: is a member of the audience making cuts?
explanation.definitionFit: A shearer cuts wool from sheep, so is literally a person who cuts.

clue.text: Glow-worm for instance chews persimmon — not quietly

indicators.note: chewing mashes the letters of the fruit into a new order
P (piano, quiet in music) is removed

explanation.surface: A glow-worm munches a persimmon in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quietly' takes P from PERSIMMON, and 'chews' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A glow-worm is a beetle, not a worm, so its name is an example of a wrong or misleading name.

clue.text: Electoral system that may provide veto?

definitions.text: Electoral system that may provide veto?

parts.words: Electoral system that may provide veto?
parts.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters of the ballot word gives veto, while the phrase names a preferential voting system

explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the four letters of the second word and you get VETO: an alternative version of it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a preferential voting system in which voters rank candidates, put to a UK referendum in 2011.

clue.text: Endless scoff dunked in sweet tea

indicators.note: the trimmed scoff word is plunged into the sweet word

parts.note: darling, like sweet, is a term of endearment

indicators.note: the last letter of the scoff word is dropped

parts.note: to jeer is to scoff

explanation.surface: Biscuits, eaten endlessly, dunked into a sweet cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops a final letter and 'dunked in' plunges the result into the endearment. 'Scoff' also means eat, which is the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Darjeeling is a fine black tea grown in the Indian hill district of that name.

clue.text: Exceeding limit and knocking someone down

definitions.meaning: running someone over is striking them with a vehicle

explanation.surface: A speeding driver goes over the limit and hits a pedestrian.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means overflowing or overrunning, and also striking a person with a car.

clue.text: Be nervous of loud organ

parts.note: F is forte, loud in music
the ear is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: A shy person is wary of a noisy church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the musical instrument, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear something is to be afraid or anxious about it.

clue.text: Shark's ear bone had to receive echo

parts.note: the malleus in the middle ear is also called the hammer

indicators.note: the word had takes in the echo letter

parts.note: E is Echo in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A shark's ear bone has picked up an echo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' puts E inside HAD to make HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammerhead is a shark named for its flattened, wide head.

clue.text: Contributed nothing new in old-fashioned surroundings

indicators.note: the old-fashioned word forms surroundings for the other pieces

parts.note: dated means out of date
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone gave nothing new, in a dated setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To have donated is to have given money or goods to a cause.

clue.text: Find divorces shattering

indicators.note: a shattered word breaks into pieces that are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A shocked discovery about how devastating divorces can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattering' rearranges the letters of 'divorces'.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to come upon or uncover it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Tinker holds a leisurely course

indicators.note: the tinker word holds the a inside it

parts.note: a tinker was a travelling mender of pots and pans

explanation.surface: A tinker keeping to a slow, wandering path.
explanation.walkthrough: A tinker was a travelling mender of pots and pans.
explanation.definitionFit: A meander is a winding bend in a river or a slow, aimless wander.

clue.text: Predecessor to Romans manages to close scripture lesson

indicators.note: the manages word closes around the lesson letters

parts.note: to fend for oneself is to manage
RI is religious instruction, the old school scripture lesson

explanation.surface: Something before Romans in the Bible manages to finish a scripture lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romans' suggests a book of the Bible, but it is Mark Antony's speech: 'Friends, Romans, countrymen'. RI is religious instruction in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Mark Antony's speech opens 'Friends, Romans, countrymen', so the word comes just before Romans.

clue.text: Seeks food a long time

definitions.meaning: an animal that ... searches for things to eat
split in two, the letters say ..., meaning a very long time

explanation.surface: An animal hunts for food for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Forages means hunts for provisions; split as two words it is an idiom for a long while.

clue.text: Chap in jumper opposing member of dynasty

indicators.note: the chap word goes in the jumper word

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, is a jumper
a chap is a man
V is versus, against

explanation.surface: A man wearing a jumper stands against a member of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, but it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romanovs were the ruling dynasty of Russia from 1613 to 1917.

clue.text: Collar's front finally black in colour

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard

indicators.note: the last letter of black goes inside the colour word

parts.note: a dye is a colouring

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of black

explanation.surface: The front of a collar is black in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives K, which 'in' puts inside DYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vandyke collar is a broad lace collar with deep points, as in portraits by van Dyck.

clue.text: Fit to be seen on road?

definitions.meaning: a fit of anger is an outburst of fury
road ... is angry behaviour by drivers

explanation.surface: Is the car roadworthy, fit to be seen on the road?
explanation.definitionFit: A fit can be a sudden attack of temper; road rage is fury shown on the road.

clue.text: Evaluation of panic rooms needing revision

indicators.note: revising the letters of the two words recasts them in a new order

explanation.surface: An assessment of secure panic rooms says they need redoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing revision' rearranges 'panic rooms'.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparison weighs things against each other, which is a kind of evaluation.

clue.text: Drama not unknown to philosopher

indicators.note: an unknown in algebra is Y, which is left out

parts.note: a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A dramatic work that is well known to a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' removes Y, a mathematical unknown, from PLAY to leave PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Socrates.

clue.text: Crazy to turn up and cause sensation

indicators.note: in a down light, turning up reads the word from the bottom

parts.note: nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: Someone acts crazily to turn up and make a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reads NUTS from the bottom in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to shock or astonish, making a sensational impression.

clue.text: Throw a match, and fail to keep it secret

definitions.meaning: a player who throws a match deliberately loses it
letting slip a secret by accident

explanation.surface: A cheat throws a match and then gives the plot away.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means reveal a secret; read literally it means hand over a contest to opponents.

clue.text: Pale and sickly, not using whole allowance

indicators.note: only part of the allowance word is used, so its inner letters are picked out

explanation.surface: Someone looks pale and ill because they did not use all their allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not using whole' takes a run of letters from inside 'allowance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wan describes a pale, unhealthy complexion.

clue.text: Holding hearts (king or queen), go down in contract

indicators.note: the go down word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: to sink is to go down
H is hearts in card notation
R stands for rex or regina, Latin king or queen

explanation.surface: A bridge player holding hearts and a royal card goes down in the contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge setting is a disguise: 'contract' is the definition, not the bid.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink is to get smaller, a direct synonym of contract.

clue.text: Shorten study, stupid

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
dense means slow-witted

explanation.surface: An editor tells someone to cut the slow-witted study.
explanation.walkthrough: To con is an old word meaning to study carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense a text is to make it shorter while keeping the substance.
